Mental Health Care Plan

Patient & GP Details
- Patient: Ayrton Warren, DOB: 16/05/1982, Gender: Not recorded, Contact: Not recorded, Address: Not recorded
- Referring GP: Not recorded, Practice: GP at Hand, Practice Address: Not recorded. Provider No.: Not recorded, Contact: Not recorded

Clinical Assessment

Identified Problems/Provisional Diagnoses:
- Principal: Acute left-sided headache — provisional tension-type headache (High likelihood); migraine considered (Medium likelihood)
- Secondary: Headache related to sleep deprivation and/or dehydration (Medium likelihood)
- Tertiary: Serious secondary causes to exclude (e.g., subarachnoid hemorrhage/intracranial bleed) — Low likelihood but considered

Clinical Details & History:
- Medications: Sertraline (dose/route/frequency not documented); Paracetamol taken this morning (dose not documented); advised to take Ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented)
- Allergies/ADRs: None known (patient reports "Not that I'm aware of")
- Past Medical History: Anxiety for approximately 2 years

Mental Health History:
- Previous Diagnoses: Anxiety (diagnosed; ongoing)
- Past Treatments (Therapy, Medications, Hospitalizations): Currently taking sertraline; no other treatments, therapy or hospitalizations documented
- Family History: Mother with history of anxiety

Social & Lifestyle Factors:
- Living Situation: Lives with partner
- Social Support: Partner present; no other supports documented
- Occupation/Education: Employed; recent increased work stress and backlog for ~2 months
- Alcohol Use: Not recorded
- Smoking/Substance Use: Non-smoker; other substance use not recorded
- Key Stressors: Work-related stress, backlog of work, repeated late nights over the past ~2 months

Mental Status Examination (MSE):
- Appearance & General Behaviour: Cooperative and engaged in consultation
- Mood & Affect: Reports not being "moody" but occasional frustration; mood described as fluctuating/ebbing and flowing
- Speech & Thought: Speech coherent and goal-directed; thought content non-psychotic
- Perception: No hallucinations or perceptual abnormalities reported

Cognition:
- Orientation: Oriented to self and date of birth as evidenced by verbal report
- Attention/Concentration: Adequate for interview (no impairment documented)
- Memory: Not formally assessed; no concerns reported
- Insight & Judgement: Appears to have insight into stressors and is receptive to advice and follow-up (e.g., agreed to counselling referral and time off work)

Physical Symptoms:
- Sleep: Recent sleep disruption with late nights; woke at ~05:30 today (usually up ~07:00); advised to target 7–8 hours/night
- Appetite: Diet described as "OK" / not unhealthy
- Motivation/Energy: Not documented beyond work-related frustration
- Anxiety Symptoms: Ongoing anxiety, particularly related to work and meeting deadlines; not currently suicidal

Risk Assessment:
- Suicidal/Self-Harm/Risk to Others: Denies thoughts of self-harm; no risk to others reported
- Protective Factors: Lives with partner, regular exercise (running ~3x/week), engaged with care, no reported substance misuse
- Overall Current Risk Level (Self): Low (based on denial of self-harm and presence of protective factors)
- Emergency Contact: Not recorded

Formulation:
- Predisposing factors: History of anxiety; family history of anxiety (mother)
- Precipitating factors: Recent increased work stress and backlog for ~2 months, late nights, acute sleep disruption this morning
- Perpetuating factors: Continued late nights, unresolved work backlog, possible inadequate hydration
- Protective factors: Partner support, regular exercise, engagement with GP, ongoing sertraline
- Integrated summary: Acute unilateral headache likely represents a primary headache disorder (tension-type and/or migraine) precipitated by prolonged work stress and sleep disturbance; dehydration and sleep deprivation may contribute. Serious secondary causes (e.g., SAH) are low probability given absence of red flags (no fever, neck stiffness, vomiting, focal neurological signs) but should be reconsidered if symptoms worsen or new features emerge.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Acute left-sided headache (provisional tension-type headache; migraine considered)
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Reduce current headache severity and associated functional impairment
  - Identify and reduce work-related triggers contributing to headaches
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Provide effective acute analgesia and supportive measures
  - Reduce precipitating stressors and improve sleep/hydration to prevent recurrence
  - Monitor for red flags and escalate investigation if no improvement
- Actions (Patient):
  - Take advised analgesia (Ibuprofen; dose/route/frequency not documented) and continue Paracetamol as needed (dose not documented)
  - Consider self-certifying time off work (suggested ~1 week) to reduce acute stress
  - Self-refer to local counselling service via provided link
  - Aim for 7–8 hours sleep per night and drink 1.5–2 L fluids daily (excluding tea/coffee)
  - Book follow-up appointment in one week or sooner if symptoms worsen or red flags develop
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Recommend acute analgesia (Ibuprofen recommended; dose/route/frequency not documented) and document in notes
  - Provide counselling referral link and instructions for self-referral
  - Advise time off work/self-certification and document recommendation
  - Provide written information on headache danger signs and advise low threshold for re-contact
  - Arrange follow-up in one week; if no improvement consider blood tests and/or neuroimaging and escalate appropriately

Secondary Problem: Anxiety disorder (ongoing; on sertraline)
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Improve management of anxiety symptoms, particularly work-related anxiety
  - Access psychological support (counselling) to develop coping strategies
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Ensure current pharmacotherapy remains effective and tolerable
  - Facilitate access to counselling/psychological therapy and monitor response
- Actions (Patient):
  - Self-refer to counselling service as advised
  - Apply stress-reduction strategies (sleep hygiene, pacing work, exercise)
  - Monitor anxiety symptoms and report any worsening or adverse effects of sertraline
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Provide counselling resource/link and consider referral options
  - Review sertraline treatment at follow-up (dose/efficacy/side effects) — sertraline dose/route/frequency not documented in current record
  - Consider formal mental health review or referral to psychological services if symptoms persist or worsen

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered:
  - Nature of probable headache types (tension-type vs migraine) and contributing factors (stress, poor sleep, dehydration)
  - Acute analgesia options (Ibuprofen recommended; dose/route/frequency not documented) and continued Paracetamol
  - Sleep hygiene (7–8 hours/night) and hydration (1.5–2 L/day)
  - Recommendation for time off work and counselling/self-referral
  - Danger signs prompting urgent review
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening:
  - New or worsening severe headache (especially sudden 'worst ever' pain)
  - Neck stiffness, fever, vomiting, focal neurological signs, loss of consciousness, progressive worsening
- Coping Strategies:
  - Rest and hydration, sleep regularization, pacing workload, regular exercise (running), counselling/psychological therapy, early re-contact with GP for worsening symptoms

Consent, Coordination & Review:
- Patient Consent to Plan: Yes — patient agreed to recommendations and to book follow-up
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: Not recorded; counselling service recommended for self-referral
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not recorded
- Review Date: Follow-up arranged in one week (patient to book appointment)

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD) — Likelihood: High
  - Justification: Documented 2-year history of anxiety, ongoing symptoms related to work stress, on sertraline.
- Adjustment disorder with anxiety (work-related) — Likelihood: Medium
  - Justification: Recent 2-month period of increased work stress, backlog and late nights precipitating symptom exacerbation; plausible acute stress-related disorder.
- Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) — Likelihood: Low
  - Justification: Depressive symptoms not reported; mood described as fluctuating with frustration but no low mood, anhedonia, or functional decline documented.

Quality checks
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs and blood pressure not recorded
  - Neurological examination and focal neurological assessment not recorded
  - Medication doses/route/frequency for sertraline, paracetamol and recommended ibuprofen not documented
  - Emergency contact details and next-of-kin not recorded
  - Formal mental health rating scales (e.g., GAD-7, PHQ-9) not recorded
- Internal conflicts between transcript and DDx:
  - None significant. (Transcript and DDx align on likely tension-type headache with consideration of migraine and low likelihood of SAH.)
- Transcript quality notes:
  - Consultation audio/dialogue largely clear; minor name confusion early in dialogue ("Atan"/"Anthony" vs "Ayrton Warren") — patient later clarifies name as Ayrton Warren.
  - No physical examination or vital signs recorded during consultation.
